Local Tastes
Tom Yum Goong
Thailand's signature hot-and-sour soup, built on river prawns, lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaf, and chili — sharp, sour, and fiery in one bowl.
Ruenthai
Som Tum
Green papaya salad pounded to order with chili, lime, fish sauce, palm sugar, and peanuts — the everyday dish Thais rate each other's cooking by.
Ruenthai
Mango Sticky Rice
Ripe mango over coconut-milk sticky rice, finished with a salty-sweet coconut sauce and toasted mung beans — the standard Thai dessert plate.
Ruenthai
Pad Thai
Rice noodles wok-fried with egg, tamarind, palm sugar, and fish sauce, topped with crushed peanuts and lime — cooked fresh at street carts across the city.
Walking Street food stalls
Food Delivery
Grab
Foreign number: accepted. — the verification code arrives by SMS on most foreign carriers, with WhatsApp offered as a fallback when the SMS is delayed.
The dominant delivery platform in Thailand and the widest restaurant coverage in Pattaya, with an English-language interface and card payment that needs no Thai bank account; peak-hour surge pricing is the main complaint.
grab.com
LINE MAN
Foreign number: not accepted. — sign-up requires a Thai mobile number for the SMS verification code; a foreign SIM is rejected at registration.
Deep restaurant coverage and tight integration with the LINE chat app locals already run their lives on, but a visitor without a Thai SIM cannot create an account at all.
lineman.line.me

Getting Around
Grab
Foreign number: accepted. — the verification code arrives by SMS on most foreign carriers, with WhatsApp offered as a fallback when the SMS is delayed.
The widest driver network in Pattaya and the most reliable option outside the Beach Road/Walking Street core; fares run 10-25% above inDrive and card payments carry a foreign-payment surcharge.
grab.com
inDrive
Foreign number: accepted. — the verification code arrives by SMS on most foreign carriers, matching sign-up reports from travellers using the app elsewhere in Thailand.
A name-your-own-fare alternative to Grab that regularly comes in cheaper for the same trip, with a smaller driver pool that can mean a longer wait late at night or outside the tourist strip; Bolt's Thailand operating licence has lapsed, leaving inDrive as the standing second option.
indrive.com

Packing for a Hike
Worth Knowing

From Fishing Village to Resort City

Pattaya was a quiet fishing village until the early 1960s, when American servicemen stationed in the region during the Vietnam War began using its beaches for rest-and-relaxation leave. The hotels, bars, and nightlife that followed grew directly out of that R&R economy, and the city has kept building on the same footprint ever since — the hard cut from fishing hamlet to resort skyline happened within a single generation.

Beach Road and Sukhumvit Road are both run by blue songthaews, shared pickup trucks known locally as baht buses. There's no schedule and no marked stop: flag one down anywhere along its route, ride in the open back with other passengers, and press the buzzer to signal a stop. The fare — 15-20 baht, paid to the driver on the way out — is separate from the Grab and inDrive apps covered under Getting Around, and often the faster option along the beachfront strip.
